title: Animal Hospital & Veterinary Clinic Facility Directory
demand_signal: Strong. Distinct from the existing 2026-05-16 'licensed-veterinarian-registry' brief — that one sells individual DVM licenses; this one sells veterinary BUSINESSES (clinic/hospital facilities), which is what equipment vendors, practice-management SaaS, pet insurance partner networks, and corporate-consolidator acquirers actually prospect. The US has ~32,000 veterinary establishments (US Census NAICS 541940). AVMA reports ~32K AAHA-eligible practices; AAHA itself has ~4,400 accredited hospitals. Commercial vendors selling this list at premium pricing: LeadsPlease ('Animal Hospitals & Veterinary Services' email list), InfoGlobalData ('Animal Hospital Email List'), BookYourData (animal hospital contacts), FrescoData, DataCaptive, LakeB2B. Major demand pull comes from veterinary corporate consolidators (Mars Veterinary Health/Banfield/VCA/BluePearl, NVA, Pathway Vet Alliance, Vetcor, PetVet Care Centers, Southern Veterinary Partners) running active M&A rollup strategies — corporate ownership of vet clinics grew from ~10% (2017) to ~25-30% (2025), with consolidator buy-side teams paying premium for clean independent-clinic lists. Pet insurance partnership programs (Trupanion, Nationwide, Healthy Paws, Pets Best, Embrace, Lemonade Pet) actively recruit clinics to their preferred-provider/direct-pay networks.
target_audience: Veterinary corporate consolidators / PE-backed rollups (Mars Veterinary Health, NVA/National Veterinary Associates, Pathway Vet Alliance, Vetcor, PetVet Care Centers, Southern Veterinary Partners, AmeriVet, Innovetive Petcare) running M&A pipelines — each independent-clinic acquisition is $1M-$15M; vet practice management software vendors (Covetrus Pulse, IDEXX Cornerstone, ezyVet, ImproMed, AVImark, Shepherd, NextGen Vet, Provet Cloud, Vetspire) selling $300-$3,000/month SaaS; veterinary diagnostic and imaging equipment vendors (IDEXX Laboratories in-house analyzers, Heska, Zomedica TRUFORMA, Antech, Sound Veterinary Ultrasound, Sound DR systems) selling $20K-$200K capex per clinic; pet insurance preferred-provider/direct-pay network programs (Trupanion Express, Nationwide, Healthy Paws, Pets Best, Embrace, Lemonade Pet, ASPCA Pet Health, Spot, MetLife Pet); veterinary pharmaceutical distributors (MWI Animal Health/Cencora, Patterson Veterinary, Henry Schein Animal Health, Covetrus distribution); AAHA accreditation sales; Fear Free certification program; veterinary lab outsourcing (Antech, IDEXX Reference Labs, Zoetis VetScan); veterinary cremation and aftercare services; CareCredit and Scratchpay clinic-financing partner enrollment; veterinary staffing/locum tenens platforms (IndeVets, Galaxy Vets, Veterinary Practice Solutions).
public_data_sources: State Veterinary Medical Boards — facility/premise permits (where states issue facility-level permits separate from individual DVM licenses)
USDA APHIS Animal Care Inspection Reports and licensed-facility list (covers some animal-care facilities)
USDA APHIS Veterinary Biologics establishment registry
CMS NPPES Type 2 NPIs filed under taxonomy 174M00000X (Veterinarian) — note: veterinary NPIs are voluntary but many file
DEA Diversion Control Active Controlled Substance Registrant lookup (clinics dispensing controlled substances have public DEA registration)
Google Maps / Google Places API (business category 'veterinary_care')
Yelp / Yellow Pages public business listings for vet clinics
AVMA accredited educational institution affiliation lists (teaching hospitals)
State Secretary of State business registry for clinic ownership entities (identifies corporate vs. independent ownership)
City and county business license registries
competitive_landscape: Moderately crowded but no flat-file SKU under $200 and none with an 'independent (non-corporate) only' filter — the highest-value segment for the consolidator buyer. LeadsPlease, InfoGlobalData, BookYourData, FrescoData, LakeB2B, and DataCaptive all sell vet-hospital lists at subscription or per-contact pricing ($1,500-$5,000/year). Specialty vertical-aware vendors (BetterVet, VetSuccess, VetLeads) exist but target consumer/owner data, not facility-level B2B. DataStructured wedge: $59-$99 per state CSV of vet clinics with corporate-ownership flag (independent / Mars-VCA-Banfield / NVA / Pathway / Vetcor / other-consolidator) — that single field is what makes the list usable for M&A pipelines, PMS sales, and equipment outreach. Competitors do not segment by ownership.
monetization_model: State-level CSVs at $59-$99 each. Fields: clinic DBA, legal entity, owner-of-record, street address, phone, website, primary DVM contact, NPI (where filed), DEA registration (where applicable), services flags (small animal / equine / exotic / emergency / surgery / dental / boarding), AAHA accreditation flag, Fear Free certification flag, corporate-ownership flag (independent vs. consolidator parent). Top-5-state bundle (CA + TX + FL + NY + PA) at $249. National independents-only bundle at $399. Premium SKU: 'Acquirable Independent Clinics — 1-3 doctor practices in top-25 metro areas' at $499 (the highest-LTV buyer is consolidator BD teams).
estimated_market_size: ~32,000 veterinary establishments in the US (NAICS 541940). ~28,000 small-animal hospitals, ~3,500 mixed/equine, ~500 specialty/emergency. Independent ownership ~70% (down from ~90% a decade ago, falling ~2% per year as consolidators acquire). Buyer LTV: consolidator acquisition = $1M-$15M per clinic; PMS SaaS = $3.6K-$36K/year; in-house diagnostic capex = $20K-$200K; pet insurance network partnership = $10K-$50K/year referral economics per clinic; veterinary distributor account = $50K-$500K/year GMV per clinic.
data_freshness_requirement: Annual updates with M&A delta updates quarterly. Consolidation churn is the key freshness driver — a clinic that was independent in Jan may be NVA-owned by Jul. Re-pulling state SoS business filings and clinic-website 'now part of [parent]' detection catches the delta.
compliance_notes: PASS. State veterinary board facility permits, USDA APHIS public records, NPPES (public organizational NPIs), DEA public registrant file, and Google Places business listings are all public. Owner-of-record from SoS filings is public corporate record. No PHI, no consumer PII. Pet owner names and animal records are explicitly excluded. Source attribution per state board URL and federal data sources.
next_steps: Harvest CMS NPPES Type 2 NPIs filtered by veterinarian taxonomy 174M00000X to get baseline universe with NPI keys
Enrich with Google Places API for clinics that don't file NPIs (NPI is voluntary for vets, so ~40% gap)

Cross-reference state Secretary of State business registry to attach legal-entity ownership; pattern-match parent-company names (Mars, VCA, Banfield, BluePearl, NVA, Pathway, Vetcor, PetVet, Southern Vet Partners, AmeriVet, Innovetive) to build corporate-ownership flag
Cross-reference AAHA public directory for accreditation flag

Launch TX independents-only SKU at $79 on Gumroad; outreach to consolidator BD teams via LinkedIn (NVA Acquisitions, Vetcor BD, etc.), PMS vendor partner channels (ezyVet, IDEXX Cornerstone), and r/veterinary practice-owner threads
researcher_notes: Distinct from the 2026-05-16 vet license brief because the buyer is fundamentally different. The vet-license brief monetizes vendors selling TO DVMs (pharma reps, CE providers). This brief monetizes vendors buying or selling FACILITIES — M&A consolidators, PMS, capex equipment, insurance networks. The corporate-ownership flag is the single differentiator that no competitor offers — and it is the EXACT field every consolidator BD team and every PMS sales team wants because (a) consolidators only target independents and (b) PMS vendors lose to lock-in if they pitch a Mars-owned clinic. Score 7 (not 8) because engineering complexity is moderate-to-high — NPI coverage is incomplete, so Google Places enrichment is required, and the corporate-ownership pattern-match is a meaningful cleaning task. Strong recurring SKU set (50 states × multiple filter cuts).
